items.text: Neutral conductor present and capped in every switch box (404.2(C)), including boxes with plain snap switches.
Switches at 48 in. to center of box where the plan is silent.
3-way/4-way runs tested from every location; load fully controlled at each switch.
No receptacle inside the tub/shower zone: 3 ft horizontal x 8 ft vertical from rim/threshold.
Exterior receptacles: WR device + in-use cover, gasket seated, cord exits the bottom notch.
Dwelling receptacles are TR type; GFI plan points are standard TR devices on the DFN breaker — no GFCI receptacles.
Replaced receptacles meet today's GFCI/AFCI/TR/WR rules for the location; no-equipment-ground installs carry the required marking.
Panel directory filled in specifically from the as-built circuits and verified by switching; spares marked as spares.
Unused panel openings closed with the panel manufacturer's listed fillers; breakers listed for the panel (Siemens new / Square D in Square D).
Sub-panels labelled with their source of supply; source panel feeder breaker labelled to match.
Bath fixtures inside the tub/shower zone are damp-listed (wet-listed if spray reaches them); no pendants in the zone.
Closet fixtures enclosed and clear of the storage space; no pendant or exposed-lamp fixtures.
Water heater circuit verified by arithmetic: nameplate amps x 1.25, breaker and conductor recorded on the panel schedule.
Microwave on its own 20A circuit, 12 AWG copper; not shared with the hood or any other appliance.
Every hard-wired appliance has its disconnect decided and reachable (water heater, cooktop, air handler).
Condenser wired from its own nameplate: conductor >= MCA, breaker <= MOCP; nameplate photographed to the job file.
HVAC disconnect within sight and readily accessible at the equipment, working space clear.
Heat strip size actually installed reported to the office for the load calc.
Motor jobs: worksheet shows table FLC and nameplate FLA separately; overload set from the nameplate.
Dwelling generator: outdoor shutdown device located, identified, and tested at start-up.
Neutrals landed one per terminal in every panelboard; doubled neutrals separated on change-outs.
Panel and HVAC equipment SCCR checked against available fault current on commercial work; both numbers in the job file.
CCA terminations checked: screw terminals only — never backstab (push-in is 14 AWG solid copper only); splices only with connectors marked CC, CC-CU, or AL/CU; 30 A+ devices marked AL/CU
